candidates: When creating new shared TypeScript modules inside the `docs/.vitepress` pipeline, name the file after the domain concept it represents (e.g., `teamMembers.ts`) rather than a generic label (e.g., `data.ts`), so the module's purpose is immediately clear to any reader.

When extracting `CoreTeam` entries (or similar data records) into a standalone module such as `teamMembers.ts`, preserve all previously explicit fields on every record — do not omit fields like `title` just because `createLinks()` or another processing function applies a `?? default` fallback. Each record should be self-documenting; relying on consumer-side defaults makes data records ambiguous and fragile to future processing changes.

When modifying the docs asset-fetching pipeline (contributor lists, avatars, etc.), add or verify a CI check that confirms the fetched assets are actually rendered/visible in the built output — not just that the fetch/download step completed without throwing an error.

In `fetch-avatars.ts` (and any future script that bulk-downloads resources from the GitHub API), avoid fully parallel requests that trigger rate-limiting: use limited concurrency or sequential downloading, include appropriate `Accept`/`User-Agent` HTTP headers, and in CI pass the `GITHUB_TOKEN` environment variable as a Bearer token to significantly raise the rate-limit ceiling.
